title: AwesomeMath Summer Program
description: AwesomeMath Summer Program is an intensive online course for mathematically talented middle and high school students (ages 12-18), covering algebra, geometry, combinatorics, and number theory at four difficulty levels aimed at competitions such as the AMC 10/12, AIME, and USA(J)MO. Each three-week session meets live Monday-Friday for a 90-minute lecture followed by a 60-minute problem-solving session, with lectures recorded, graded daily homework, and twice-weekly office hours. Students can enroll in one, two, or all three sessions, which run June 8-26, June 29-July 17, and July 20-August 7, 2026. New applicants must create an account, submit an online application and teacher recommendation, and complete an untimed, unproctored admission test; returning students and USA(J)MO qualifiers are automatically admitted.
selectivity_evidence: New applicants must create an account, complete an online application, obtain a teacher recommendation, and submit an untimed, unproctored admission test; AwesomeMath states returning students and USA(J)MO qualifiers are automatically admitted, indicating a real screening step for new applicants rather than open enrollment. No acceptance rate is published.

title: Rutgers Young Scholars Program in Discrete Mathematics
description: The Rutgers Young Scholars Program in Discrete Mathematics is a four-week, in-person residential summer program on Rutgers' Busch campus, run through DIMACS since 1990 (with two exceptions) for mathematically talented high school students. Roughly 30 students per year work with Rutgers faculty and undergraduate teaching assistants on a problem-solving-focused introduction to discrete mathematics rather than straight lecture instruction. Participants live in an air-conditioned residence hall Monday through Friday and return home each weekend during the four-week session. Applicants must solve a set of mathematical problems as part of the admission process and submit a teacher recommendation and high school transcript, with the program explicitly encouraging applications from females and students from underrepresented groups in the mathematical sciences.
residency_restrictions: International students are not eligible for the program's scholarship/financial aid funding, though the page does not state they are barred from the program itself.
application_requirements: solutions to a mathematical problem set
selectivity_evidence: Applicants must solve a set of assigned mathematical problems (partial solutions accepted) as part of admission, and the program selects approximately 30 students annually; applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis rather than open enrollment. No formal acceptance rate is published on the official page.

title: Carnegie Mellon SAMS (Summer Academy for Math and Science)
description: Carnegie Mellon's Summer Academy for Math and Science (SAMS) is a fully funded, six-week residential pre-college program for rising high school seniors, run in three parts: a virtual jumpstart (June 15-16, 2026), a six-week in-person session on CMU's Pittsburgh campus (June 20-August 1, 2026) combining a rigorous math and science curriculum with faculty-advised STEM research projects, weekly college-application writing workshops, and a credit-bearing 'Student to Scholar' course, and a follow-on virtual engagement phase covering FAFSA, college prep, and budgeting. Coursework spans areas such as game theory, biochemistry/molecular biology/forensics, and analytical chemistry techniques, supported by mentoring groups and academic coaching. Students present their research at a final symposium open to families. There is no tuition cost to admitted students; travel to and from Pittsburgh is the student's own responsibility, and financial documentation is required as part of the application.
citizenship_restrictions: U.S. citizen or permanent resident required.
application_requirements: two recommendation letters (one from current math instructor)
financial documentation (tax documents or NACAC fee waiver)
selectivity_evidence: CMU describes admission as a holistic review considering 'a combination of factors' and specifically encourages applications from underrepresented STEM students, including first-generation college students and those from under-resourced high schools; the program is fully funded and merit-based rather than open enrollment. No acceptance rate is published on the official page.

title: Secondary Student Training Program (SSTP)
description: The Secondary Student Training Program (SSTP) is a highly selective, five-and-a-half-week residential summer research program hosted by the University of Iowa's Belin-Blank Center for students in grades 10-11. Participants conduct original research under the mentorship of a University of Iowa faculty member, attend classes and seminars, and produce a research brief and academic poster presented at the program's conclusion; successful completion earns 3 semester hours of University of Iowa credit. The 2026 session runs June 17-July 24, 2026. Selection prioritizes essay quality and content, followed by transcripts and test scores, recommendation letters, and alignment of a student's research interests with available faculty mentors; both U.S. and international students may apply, with international applicants required to show English proficiency.
application_requirements: two letters of reference (academic and character)
proof of English proficiency for international students

title: BU RISE (Research in Science & Engineering)
description: BU RISE places rising high school seniors directly into Boston University research settings for a six-week program with two tracks. The Internship Track has students conduct 40 hours a week of individual research under faculty, postdoctoral, or graduate-student mentorship in fields such as astronomy, biology, biomedical/electrical/mechanical engineering, chemistry, computer science, neuroscience, physics, psychology, and public health. The Practicum Track combines morning lectures with four hours of daily group research in either Computational Neurobiology or Data Science. Both tracks culminate in a Poster Symposium plus weekly professional-development workshops. The 2026 program runs June 28-August 7 (residential) or June 29-August 7 (commuter), and is limited to U.S. citizens and legal permanent residents; Internship Track admission requires a faculty member to agree to host the student as an intern after an initial review, while Practicum Track applicants receive a direct decision for their first-choice course.
citizenship_restrictions: U.S. citizens and legal permanent residents only.
application_requirements: financial aid documents if applying for aid
selectivity_evidence: BU's own admissions page describes a two-stage process for the Internship Track: applicants pass an initial review and then enter a faculty-matching phase where, per the official page, 'you will only receive an offer of admission if a faculty member agrees to host you as an intern' (unmatched applicants may be waitlisted); Practicum Track applicants receive direct decisions for their first-choice course with limited space for a second choice.
